Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

survive verb

also survival, survivor, outlive, live on, come through alive

classical

Cic. N.D. 2.72: ut suī sibi līberī superstitēs essent (Lewis & Short)
Tac. Agr. 46.4

superstes, superstitis

adjective, one ending, with esse; the person or thing outlived in the dative (less often the genitive) · Wiktionary

surviving, outliving

The usual way to say survive: superstes esse alicui, to outlive someone; superstes alone, a survivor. Of things too: a name or a book that lives on (Tacitus, below).

Other words

  • supersum, superesse, superfuī — be left; survive, outlive

    irregular verb (sum), with dative · also used · classical · Liv. 1.34: Lucumō superfuit patrī (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 1.26: circiter mīlia hominum CXXX superfuērunt · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Chiefly to be left over (see remain); of people, to be still alive after others are dead, as Caesar counts the survivors of a battle. Lewis & Short calls the sense rare.

  • salūs, salūtis f. — survival, safety, being saved

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Declension on Wiktionary

    For “survival” as an abstract noun: dē salūte agitur, survival is at stake. Of a person who comes through unharmed, incolumis (Cic. Cat. 3.10 fin., integrōs incolumēsque, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Agricola posteritātī narrātus et trāditus superstes erit

    Agricola, told and handed down to those who come after, will surviveTac. Agr. 46.4

  • ut suī sibi līberī superstitēs essent

    that their children should outlive themCic. N.D. 2.72 (Lewis & Short)

See also remain, escape, exist.
